column17: Possibly a pause between release cycles.
column23: The Oct 2023 to Jun 2025 gap is clear but unexplained. Issue #127 and four other gap-period issues did not lead to public activity until the June 2025 MRtrix3 upgrade and 0.6.0 release. The same maintainer returned, suggesting a maintenance pause rather than a documented handoff.

Activity is continuous at the multi-month scale with no gaps of at least three months. The recorded maximum is a one-month lull, so there is no convincing inactivity episode to explain. The July 2025 README update and PR #347 show maintenance continuing rather than a distinct revival.

column19: Version 0.0.3 changelog update after the gap.
column23: The four-month early-project gap is moderately easy to locate but its cause is not recorded. The work before it added parameterized intervals and root-finding while the first commit after it updated the 0.0.3 changelog, making a release-cycle pause plausible but unproven. The project subsequently developed substantial long-term activity.

column17: Possibly a temporary maintainer bandwidth pause.
column19: JAX-related numerical jitter prompted tolerance updates (Sep 2024).
column23: The roughly five-month interval is visible in the commit history but its cause is not documented. README version updates frame the pause, and the return commit specifically addresses numerical jitter introduced by a new JAX version. The same maintainer resumed the project.

column17: Possibly a temporary maintainer bandwidth pause.
column23: The recorded three-month gap in June-August 2022 is easy to identify, but issue #302 and #303 and the README history do not establish its cause. Activity resumed with corot's action error-range change and PR #304, showing contributor continuity rather than a handoff. A second three-month zero-commit interval occurred in Jan-Mar 2025, so the timeseries has a tie for the longest gap.

column17: Possibly an early contributor availability pause.
column19: Double scalar conversion bug fix marked return (Mar 2014).
column23: The roughly 32-month gap is easy to identify but hard to interpret because no nearby issue, PR, or README evidence explains it. The first return commit fixes a conversion error and later activity focuses on compatibility and release maintenance. The author changed from Martin Ling to James McFlan, indicating a contributor handoff rather than a documented recovery plan.

column19: Issue #122 prompted T2 support, PR #125 fixed an example.
column23: The 13-month gap is easy to see, but the commit and issue evidence does not explain why work stopped. The return is clearer: issue #122 requested T2 diagnostics and the Aug 2020 commit added support for it, followed by an example correction. Later history shows both maintainer work and automated dependency updates.

column19: Typo fix and PR #51, alongside example updates (Aug 2024).
column20: Michael Klots (new contributor), Rajesh Singh (old maintainer)
column23: The year-long gap is apparent but difficult to explain because the commit subjects are often terse and no record establishes why development stopped. Typo-related PRs #49-#51 preceded the Aug 2024 return, including an open code-quality issue, and activity resumed with both Michael Klots and Rajesh Singh. The latest commit remains Aug 31, 2024, so the project is inactive under the 2025-09-30 cutoff rule.

column19: Quantile harmonization (Nov 2024), then an n.quantiles option (Mar 2025).
column23: The nine-month gap is identifiable but its cause remains uncertain despite issue and PR activity during the interval. Work resumed with quantile harmonization in bias correction and another quantile-related change in March 2025, showing maintenance rather than a clearly documented revival. The last commit predates April 1, 2025, so the project is inactive.

column17: Possibly reduced maintainer availability despite open issues.
column19: Graviton2 build work and documentation/build PRs resumed (Mar 2022).
column23: The 26-month gap is clear but hard to interpret because many issues accumulated without regular commits. The first return work targeted Graviton2 compatibility, alongside PRs fixing documentation and compilation, yet the public record does not say what caused the quiet period. New contributors took part in the return and later maintenance, and activity continued past the cutoff.
